September 21, 2024 — You focused on finalizing Soneva Jani: six nights costing $10,800. You described the resort confirmation as 90% complete, sought the final email, and reviewed the overall trip budget before committing everything.
September 22, 2024 — You worked on the Trans Maldivian Airways transfer: a $1,000 round-trip fare for two, with your spouse preferring a 9 AM departure. The airline responded within two hours, which reassured you, and you planned around reaching check-in at 7:30 AM.
September 23, 2024 — Your $450 Allianz insurance plan was fully in place. You reviewed coverage and the claims process, including Mark’s assurance about processing within 10 business days, while also checking transfer vouchers and how to verify the $1,000 seaplane payment through your MasterCard account.
September 24, 2024 — You refined the itinerary together, including moving snorkeling from day 3 to day 4. You also worked through confirmations, travel documents, emergency information, and task priorities to reduce last-minute overwhelm, and considered how to use your newly purchased travel journal.
September 25, 2024 — Packing became a major focus: you reported being 70% done and aimed to finish within 48 hours, later referring to a 36-hour reminder. You reviewed the seaplane’s stated 20 kg luggage limit, footwear, evening outfits, toiletries, electronics, and document backups. Your clothing-packing status was inconsistent—you later said no clothing or swimsuits had been packed—so completion cannot be established. You were also finalizing lecture-note handover to a colleague.
September 26, 2024 — You and your spouse had a joint pre-trip health appointment arranged at City Health Clinic. Following Trevor’s suggestion, you planned to call about hepatitis A vaccination and check insurance coverage; the evidence does not confirm that you received the vaccine. You also worked on rescheduling university commitments.
September 27, 2024 — You turned to verifying automated work and home arrangements for your absence, checking how to ensure those systems were correctly set up rather than leaving them untested.
September 28, 2024 — You gave mental preparation more attention because leaving everything behind felt stressful. You chose Calm, initially planning to try its free content, planned to limit news checks to five minutes daily, and explored meditation, journaling, seaplane visualization, and a backup chat with Melissa for unexpected anxiety.
September 29, 2024 — You continued final confirmations, retaining the 9 AM seaplane plan and seeking written confirmation of Soneva Jani’s 2 PM check-in. You also organized printed and digital paperwork, monitored the weather forecast, and prepared to formally confirm your 15-day university absence.
September 30, 2024 — You double-checked that your university email autoresponder was active and revisited how to make the most of the nine relaxation days you had planned.
October 1, 2024 — Planning shifted toward settling in and managing jet lag. You wanted to use the resort’s 24-hour concierge service for local recommendations, activity planning, and advance reservations to reduce the practical burden on you.
October 2, 2024 — Your spouse proposed a 6 AM sunrise photo shoot on the villa deck. You planned to ask Nimal about a customized itinerary, honeymoon packages, spa treatments, unique dining, and booking times. You also worked on confirming a planned $50 couples’ massage at So Spa while protecting your relaxation goals.
October 3, 2024 — You continued shaping a gentle stay around meditation, pool time, comfortable walking routes, and mild food options, including a no-spice salad at Crab Shack. Importantly, you clarified that you had not made any dinner reservations, so the earlier discussion of a dinner being moved to 7:30 PM should not be treated as a confirmed arrangement.
